question: What is the primary definition of an unsafe abortion according to global health standards?

options.A: A surgical procedure performed strictly in a teaching hospital
options.B: Any termination requested by a patient under the age of eighteen
options.C: Any pregnancy loss occurring naturally during the first trimester
options.D: A termination done by unskilled persons or in substandard environments

explanation: Unsafe abortion specifically refers to procedures executed by people without proper training or in places lacking minimal medical safety standards. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h1)

question: Why do many Nigerian women seek clandestine abortion services despite known health risks?

options.A: Restrictive legal frameworks and heavy social stigma surrounding the practice
options.B: A widespread preference for traditional herbal mixtures over modern surgery
options.C: Free availability of safe surgical options in private rural clinics
options.D: Direct encouragement from community healthcare workers in primary centers

explanation: Stigma, cost, and legal restrictions force vulnerable women to use unsafe, underground providers. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h1)

question: What causes internal organ damage when sharp instruments are used during an unsafe abortion?

options.A: Sudden electrolyte imbalance from excessive intravenous fluid loss
options.B: Immediate renal failure caused by rapid blood pressure drops
options.C: Perforation of the uterine wall leading to visceral injury
options.D: Complete obstruction of the upper gastrointestinal tract

explanation: Unskilled instrument insertion easily breaches the muscular wall of the uterus, risking damage to adjacent organs like the bladder or bowel. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h2)

question: How do harsh chemical substances used in some abortion attempts cause harm to the body?

options.A: They selectively block pain receptors without affecting local tissues
options.B: They immediately neutralize all bacterial pathogens in the pelvic cavity
options.C: They induce localized tissue death and severe chemical inflammation
options.D: They stimulate rapid contraction of the cervix to expel the fetus safely

explanation: Caustic substances burn delicate vaginal and cervical tissues, causing tissue breakdown and widespread toxicity in the body. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h2)

question: What is a main clinical sign that a patient has developed a pelvic infection following an unsafe abortion?

options.A: Uncontrolled involuntary movements of the lower limbs
options.B: Foul-smelling vaginal discharge and pelvic pain
options.C: Sudden and severe reduction in resting heart rate
options.D: Extreme elevation of red blood cell counts

explanation: Infection inside the damaged uterine environment produces a characteristic foul-smelling discharge, fever, and lower abdominal pain. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h3)

question: Which complication is most directly linked to incomplete evacuation of the products of conception?

options.A: Chronic obstruction of the respiratory airways
options.B: Permanent paralysis of the lower extremities

explanation: Retained tissue prevents the uterus from contracting effectively, resulting in continuous and potentially life-threatening bleeding. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h3)

question: What is the first priority when checking an unstable patient who just had an unsafe abortion?

options.B: Stabilizing the airway, breathing, and circulation
options.D: Obtaining a detailed legal history of the procedure

explanation: Emergency care always begins with checking vital life support systems to ensure the patient is stable. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h4)

question: A patient has severe lower abdominal tenderness, guarding, and rebound pain after an abortion. What condition should the nurse suspect?
explanation: Abdominal guarding and rebound pain are classic signs pointing toward infection of the lining of the abdomen or a hole in an organ. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h4)

question: Which medication do nurses commonly give to help the uterus contract during heavy bleeding after an abortion?
explanation: Uterotonics like oxytocin and misoprostol help the muscle of the uterus contract, clamping down on bleeding blood vessels. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h5)

question: Why is it essential to closely monitor urine output in a patient with severe bleeding after an abortion?

options.A: To measure the exact volume of intravenous antibiotics given
options.B: To assess the breakdown of pain medications
options.C: To evaluate kidney function and prevent kidney failure
options.D: To confirm the complete cessation of internal bladder bleeding

explanation: Severe blood loss reduces blood flow to the kidneys, making urine output a direct sign of how well fluid resuscitation is working. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h5)

question: What is the main goal of comprehensive Post-Abortion Care (PAC) in nursing?

options.A: Providing holistic medical, emotional, and contraceptive support
options.C: Restricting future access to all gynecological services
options.D: Reporting the patient immediately to local law enforcement

explanation: Post-Abortion Care includes emergency medical treatment, family planning counseling, and emotional support without judgment. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h6)

question: How does non-judgmental nursing communication help a patient recovering from an unsafe abortion?

options.A: It removes the need for any physical health checks
options.B: It builds trust and encourages the patient to return for follow-up care
options.C: It legally excuses the hospital from recording the complication
options.D: It speeds up the surgical healing of any uterine holes

explanation: Compassionate, stigma-free care helps patients feel safe, which improves their willingness to accept counseling and follow-up medical visits. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h6)
